original_question: Which two-parameter Poisson brackets {·,·}_{a,ρ} on R^3 remain invariant under a fixed Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry, meaning Q({·,·}_{a,ρ})≡0 at every point? More generally, which Poisson bi-vectors P satisfy both the Jacobi identity [[P,P]]=0 and the invariance condition Q(P)=0 for a chosen symmetry Q?
target_in_paper: The closest paper-faithful target is the open-problem theme in arXiv:1910.05844 concerning the action of a fixed Kontsevich graph-cocycle symmetry on a known class of Poisson brackets, specifically asking for those brackets on which the induced infinitesimal flow vanishes identically; in the R^3 case singled out by the draft, this means the Nambu/Jacobian class P(rho,[a]) rather than an unrestricted classification of all Poisson bivectors.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the fixed-point condition Q(P)=0 for a chosen Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry and correctly rewrites the Poisson condition as the Jacobi equation [[P,P]]=0 for a bivector P. It also points in the right direction by singling out the R^3 family governed by a Casimir-type function a and a density rho.
missing_details: In the paper, Q is not an arbitrary operator: it is a Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry Q=Or(gamma) obtained from a chosen graph cocycle gamma.
The ambient setting is that of finite-dimensional affine manifolds over R with smooth Poisson bivectors, not an unspecified algebraic or formal setting.
On R^3 the relevant family is the Nambu/Jacobian class {f,g}_{rho,a}=rho(x,y,z) det(partial(a,f,g)/partial(x,y,z)); a and rho are arbitrary smooth functions, not two scalar parameters.
If one works in bivector language, the question should name the associated bivector P(rho,[a]) explicitly and say that Q acts on bivectors via the graph-orientation morphism.
The vanishing condition must be stated globally: Q(P)=0 means the resulting bivector field is identically zero on all of R^3, not just at a point or on a leaf.

Within the Nambu/Jacobian class, the Jacobi identity is part of the class definition in the paper's discussion of known Poisson brackets, so the draft's broad 'find all P with [[P,P]]=0 and Q(P)=0' is wider than the paper's actual scope.
The paper frames this as an open problem about the action of known symmetries on known classes of Poisson brackets; it does not ask for a full classification over all Poisson manifolds.
To make the R^3 question sharp, one must fix the symmetry in advance, e.g. the flow coming from a specific graph cocycle such as the tetrahedral cocycle.
refined_question: Fix a Kontsevich graph cocycle gamma and the corresponding infinitesimal symmetry Q=Or(gamma) acting on Poisson bivectors on affine manifolds. For the Nambu/Jacobian Poisson brackets on R^3, given by {f,g}_{rho,a}(x,y,z)=rho(x,y,z) det(partial(a,f,g)/partial(x,y,z)) with a,rho in C^infty(R^3) and associated bivector P(rho,[a]), determine those pairs (rho,a) for which the bracket is stationary under the chosen Kontsevich flow, i.e. Q(P(rho,[a])) is identically zero as a bivector field on R^3. Equivalently, within this known class of Poisson brackets, characterize the fixed points of the chosen Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry.
justification: arXiv:1910.05844 is a short open-problems note, not a theorem paper with numbered Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3. The draft is therefore best matched not to a numbered statement, but to the paper's 'known classes of Poisson brackets' agenda: studying how a fixed Kontsevich graph-flow behaves on special classes and, in particular, when that flow vanishes identically. Your first sentence is close to that intent, but it needs the paper's actual class P(rho,[a]) on affine R^3 and the fact that Q must come from a chosen graph cocycle. Your second sentence broadens too far beyond the paper by asking for all Poisson bivectors P on arbitrary spaces; the note stays narrower and problem-driven.
